title: How to use AI for marketing
description: Connect audience insights, campaign planning, content, and performance learning without losing the brand or the reasoning between steps.
introduction: Marketing teams rarely struggle for lack of ideas. The harder part is keeping audience insights, campaign decisions, content, and results connected when the work moves across analytics, ad platforms, customer conversations, documents, and the live web.

Strawberry works across those tabs and tools. Your companion can inspect the current sources, keep proof close to the claim it supports, and carry an accepted audience or campaign decision into the next piece of work. As you correct it, it can also remember the sources, definitions, and brand choices your team trusts.

sections.title: What Strawberry can help you do

items.title: Understand the audience and market
items.description: Bring customer evidence, competitor activity, and search behavior into a clearer view.

items.title: Plan the campaign
items.description: Choose the objective, audience, proposition, channels, measurement, and work required.

items.title: Build the content system
items.description: Turn the strategy into themes, briefs, owners, cadence, and realistic production.

items.title: Create and adapt the content
items.description: Produce the anchor piece, then reshape the idea and proof for each channel.

items.title: Learn from performance

blocks.text: Not sure where to begin? Your companion can look at the marketing work you have open and suggest a useful skill to try first.

skill.context: Choose and complete the marketing workflow that would help most right now.

blocks.text: Useful audience research shows what people are trying to do, how they describe the problem, what changes their behavior, and where the evidence is still thin. Strawberry can bring together interviews, support conversations, reviews, communities, analytics, search behavior, and campaign results while keeping the important examples linked to their sources.

items.title: Research the audience
items.text: Turn approved customer and market sources into a linked view of needs, language, behavior, channels, tensions, and gaps—without turning the work into a contact list.

skill.context: Turn approved customer and market evidence into a source-linked audience view.

items.title: See how competitors are making the case
items.text: Compare current positioning, messaging, offers, channels, and proof around a real marketing decision.

skill.context: Compare competitors around a real positioning, campaign, product, or market decision.

items.title: Find the organic-search opportunity
items.text: Connect search demand, intent, current performance, the live site, and competitive difficulty to an action plan.

skill.context: Turn organic-search evidence into a prioritized action plan.

sections.title: Turn the evidence into a campaign plan

blocks.text: A campaign plan should make the choices visible: what the team wants to change, who the work is for, what it will offer or say, which channels have a real job, what needs to be made, and how the team will know whether it worked. Strawberry can use the audience evidence, earlier campaigns, brand material, product facts, competitor activity, performance data, and current channel context without flattening them into one generic brief.

items.context: Build the evidence into an approval-ready campaign plan without launching it.

blocks.text: A content plan is more useful than a full calendar when it explains why each theme and format exists, which evidence supports it, who owns it, and what the team can realistically produce. Strawberry can connect those choices to the audience and campaign evidence while finding useful source material and opportunities to reuse work the team already has.

items.context: Turn the strategy and evidence into themes, briefs, owners, cadence, and reuse.

blocks.text: Once a brief is ready, Strawberry can work beside the source material, earlier content, brand guidance, campaign plan, and the channel where the piece will live. It can create the anchor asset and then reshape the angle, structure, depth, proof, and call to action for a blog post, email, social post, landing page, or another format.

items.context: Create source-grounded content and useful channel-specific variants.

blocks.text: Marketing performance is easier to act on when the definitions come before the conclusions. Strawberry can compare periods, audiences, funnel stages, attribution windows, spend, creative, and channel results across the tools that hold them. It keeps observed change separate from a plausible explanation, so a useful review can end with a better decision or test instead of a confident story the data cannot support.

items.context: Reconcile the evidence, explain the changes that matter, and recommend the next decision or experiment.

blocks.text: As you correct real work, your companion can remember which sources you trust, how you define the funnel, what counts as sufficient proof, and how the brand should sound. The next brief or review can start from those accepted choices instead of a generic template.

items: Share an approved result when someone only needs the artifact.
Set up a shared team workflow when people need the same sources, judgment, ownership, and review points.
Create a Routine after the trigger, destination, and expected review are clear.

items.context: Turn a proven marketing method into a shared workflow with clear ownership and boundaries.

blocks.text: Start with the marketing question that matters now. The system becomes valuable as audience evidence, campaign choices, content, and learning stop being rebuilt from scratch.
